questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere with a possibilty for sports oriented classes, and a place where I understood the local language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, as they sent all relevant information through emails or pointed to where infomation could be found, both online and in-person.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was some general orientation and tours around campus and the city, to get a general feel and understanding for the area and university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find housing, that had leasing plans that only lasted for a semester. I managed to find a couple through a website provided by the university for off-campus housing, and made a few phone calls prior to arriving, in order to find where I eventually lived. I would recommend to start early with the search for housing, as it is a difficult market to find a place to live

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The public transportation is really good, and that the city is very walkable, so most places are only around 15 minutes from campus and the center of the city

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was done through a course search and enrollment system, where you were able to see the schdule for your courses, along with exam dates and workload. Once you found the courses, you simply added them to the basket, and then you got a email, that you were enrolled

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can either call, email or go to the offices for help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do the registration as soon as possible, to make sure you get the courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took primarly introductionary courses or lower level courses, as I wanted the possibilty to explore and experience in and around Madison, as well as travel.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite similar in some courses in terms of structure, with lectures and class disscussions, while the teaching style in some of the courses be more like high school style, with roll-call and homework.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Anthro 100: General Anthropology
History 136: Sport, recreation & society in the United States
Kines 123: Living well: Lifestyle redesign and health promotion for college students
Scand St 250: Introduction to Scandinavia

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
History 136: Sport, recreation & society in the United States
It is a very interesting and eye-opening course, and highligts how important sports is for USA history

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In general, Madison is quite expensive, both in terms of rent and daily goods, like groceries-

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive then I though

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a bunch of social/sporting clubs, with the subjects being both academic and non-academic in nature (there was a cheese club, that was very popular), as well as a bunch of different sports game happening, for example, American football, volleyball, soccer, basketball.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to as many different sports games as possible

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are a bunch of good minor/major hiking routes around Madison and Wisconsin, go to Chicago/Milwaukee, do roadtrips to other close states and the local airport is very well connected, so there is a good oppotunity to see the entire USA

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, as people were welcoming and open for talking with people

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the social clubs, as a way to meet people outside of the classroom

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was anything that I found challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the helpfulness of the local community, espically in explaining different traditions for the school, and the importance of them

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Go to as many different sports games as possible
2. You will find a place to live, even if it takes some time to find
3. Pack proper winter clothes, as it does get down to -20 during the winter

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The different sports games and experiences around the games, espically the College football games and volleyball games

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a place to live

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
